message.content:
The famous scene where Del Boy falls through the bar appears in the **Only Fools and Horses** episode titled **"Yuppy Love"**. This was the first episode of **Series 6**, which originally aired on **January 8, 1989** on BBC1.

In this iconic scene, Del Boy (played by Sir David Jason) and Trigger (played by Roger Lloyd Pack) are in a trendy wine bar trying to impress two women. Del tells Trigger to "play it nice and cool, son, nice and cool," but as he goes to lean on the bar, he doesn't notice the barman has lifted the counter hatch, and he falls straight through to the floor. Trigger, in his typical fashion, looks around completely bemused, wondering where Del has disappeared to.

The scene has been voted the funniest moment in British sitcom history multiple times. Interestingly, it was almost quite different — Sir David Jason insisted on making the fall more dramatic than writer John Sullivan originally envisioned (Sullivan had wanted Del to just stumble and catch himself). Additionally, Trigger wasn't originally scripted to be in the scene; Roger Lloyd Pack apparently turned up unannounced on the filming day, and John Sullivan decided to include him, with Trigger's confused reaction adding significantly to the comedy.

The episode also features Rodney meeting Cassandra Parry at evening classes for the first time, and Del adopting a yuppie image with Filofax and briefcase.
